messages:
Hector (People Ops): Quick Q from Ben (new hire): they receive a small monthly "micro-stipend" for pager duty (~$40) and will start unpaid parental leave mid-month. Theyd like to keep $30 of the micro-stipend going to their 401(k) and HSA if possible. Any special steps?

Ben (New Hire): yup want to keep contributing if its allowed.

Rina (Payroll): Short: micro-stipends can be treated as eligible wages but we need to code them properly. Use payroll earnings code STIP_MICRO (taxable). If posted as STIP_MICRO in a pay period with taxable wages, our engine will apply the employees 401(k) election to it. HSA pre-tax will also apply only when taxable wages exist that payroll can deduct from.

Rina (Payroll): Important operational notes: 1) Submit a payroll change ticket via Service Portal at least 72 hours before the pay date and request STIP_MICRO be included for the pay period. 2) If you want a special one-off election (only the stipend, not base salary), include that in the ticket. 3) Recordkeeper file exports go out on pay+2 business days; changes must be in payroll before cutoff to flow to vendor.

Hector (People Ops): Any vendor minimums? $30 might be small.

Rina (Payroll): Most vendors accept small amounts. For this company plan the recordkeeper has a $20 per-contribution minimum; Ill confirm and post proof. If vendor rejects, employee can make a direct HSA contribution and claim it on Form 8889.

Benefits Bot: Added internal KB link: benefits.kb/micro-stipend-deferrals.

Rina (Payroll): Action: Ill confirm vendor min and then publish a 2-line KB: "How to defer micro-stipends into 401(k)/HSA while on unpaid leave" with the STIP_MICRO code and the 72-hour ticket instruction. Tagging @Hector for review.

Ben (New Hire): thanks all, that helps.

Hector (People Ops): cheers :thumbsup:

(End of thread)
